sheet-23-1.description: Main part of sheet 23 of the 1917 Sanborn atlas of Garfield, covering the north-west of the borough of Wallington at 100 feet to an inch; the sheet's arrows point about 12 degrees west of true north. It shows the regular grid between the Passaic River, which curves along the top and down the west side opposite the City of Passaic, and Lodi Av: Parkway, Lester and Mercer crossed by Scott Av, Van Winkle Av, Anderson Av, Maple Av, Hayward, Wallington Av, Halstead Av and Hatheway. At the river's edge stand the Passaic Lumber Co. box factory with its lumber piles and a wooden pier, and a note marks a pumping station to be erected. The Ulma Park Casino dance hall stands west of Van Winkle Av near the steel bridge that carries Lodi Av over the river. The northern blocks are largely vacant lots; south of Lester the blocks fill with frame dwellings and some stores, many of them tenements. Below Lodi Av, east of Maple Av, the part continues south over the diagonal blocks of Maple Av, Hayward Pl and Wallington Av to Union Pl and the bend of Hatheway, more densely built with dwellings, stores and a few auto garages. Two separately framed insets at the foot of the sheet (River Rd, and Lodi Av at Hatheway) are separate parts.
notes: Lodi Av. is today Main Avenue; Hatheway is Hathaway Street; Union Pl. is Union Boulevard.
Scott Av. is not in OpenStreetMap.
The Main Avenue / Maple Avenue junction was rejected (7.6 m): Maple Av. bends at Lodi Av. on the sheet.
Firms: Passaic Lumber Co. (box manufacturing); Ulma Park Casino dance hall.

Garfield volume sheet 23 (Wallington), 100 ft to an inch; arrows point about 12 deg west of true north. Three parts: part 1 main map (Parkway, Lester, Mercer, Lodi Av between Scott Av and Hatheway, and south of Lodi Av east of Maple Av to Union Pl); part 2 inset lower left (River Rd and Carleton Av, Hemion Coal & Grain Co.); part 3 inset lower middle (Lodi Av at Hatheway by the Passaic River, Pure Oil Co.).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: River Rd and Carleton Av, Hemion Coal & Grain Co. by the Passaic River (one doubtful junction: modern Carlton Avenue meets River Street there, but the drawn River Rd runs north-east where no modern street does, and the inset's arrow and the modern bearings disagree by 20 to 30 degrees; needs hand-picked control, or carried points from Garfield sheet 27 (not in this record)).

sheet-23-3.description: Small framed inset at the foot of sheet 23 of the 1917 Sanborn atlas of Garfield, in Wallington, showing Lodi Av where Hatheway crosses it beside a bend of the Passaic River. Hatheway runs straight north from Lodi Av and bends to the south-east below it. North of Lodi Av between Hatheway and the river are a row of vacant lots and the Pure Oil Co. oils and gasoline plant with its tanks and a night watchman; south of Lodi Av are two frame dwellings and a larger building on block 38. It is drawn at the sheet's 100 feet to an inch with its own arrow pointing up the page, which like the sheet's main arrow is about 12 degrees off true north.
notes: Lodi Av. is today Main Avenue; Hatheway is Hathaway Street.
Placed from the single junction Hathaway Street / Main Avenue with the atlas scale and the main part's rotation assumed; low confidence.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 of the 1917 Sanborn atlas of Garfield, covering a block of Wallington at 50 feet to an inch, larger than the neighbouring sheets, and turned so that north points about 31 degrees clockwise of up. It shows the area between Lodi Av (Lodi Road) at the top and Union Pl at the foot, from Paterson Av along the Passaic River to Maple Av. Most of the large western block is the Anderson Lumber Co. planing mill and packing case factory, with planing and sawing rooms, lumber sheds and three numbered lumber yards; another arm of its lumber yard lies between Paterson Av and the river. Along Anderson Av and Maple Av are rows of frame dwellings, some stuccoed or plastered, an auto and plumbing shop, and the yard of Wm. De Vogel, building contractor. River Rd branches from Paterson Av at the left edge, and the line between Wallington and East Rutherford is marked along Paterson Av. A notes box describes the lumber company's fire protection.
notes: Lodi Av. (Lodi Road) is today Main Avenue; Union Pl. is Union Boulevard; River Rd. appears to be the north part of today's Carlton Avenue.
The Main Avenue / Paterson Avenue junction was rejected (18.6 m); Paterson Avenue's modern line runs west of the drawn street.
Drawn at 50 ft to an inch, unlike sheets 23, 25 and 26.

Garfield volume sheet 24 (Wallington), 50 ft to an inch (scale of feet), turned (north about 31 deg clockwise). One part: Lodi Av (Lodi Road) south to Union Pl between Paterson Av and Maple Av; Anderson Lumber Co. planing mill and yards; River Rd at the left edge.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 of the 1917 Sanborn atlas of Garfield, covering central and southern Wallington at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points about 36 degrees clockwise of up. It runs from Union Pl at the top to the vacant tracts beyond James and King, between Paterson Av on the East Rutherford line and Tuttle. Streets are Bond, Dankhoff Av, Locust Av, William and James crossing Maple Av, Hayward Pl, Wallington Av, Koster, Hatheway and 1st St, with Wallington Pl, Locust Pl and May near Lodi Av in the north-east corner. The north part is closely built with frame dwellings and stores, and holds the Wallington Public School No. 1, the fire department and Wallington Hose Co. No. 1, the Wallington Presbyterian Church, two handkerchief embroidering shops, and the Henry W. Plant & Co. curtain and robe factory near the Passaic River. The southern third is laid out in lots but almost empty (block 49). Across Paterson Av the ends of East Rutherford's streets are lettered.
notes: Union Pl. is today Union Boulevard; James is Pulaski Avenue; Hatheway is Hathaway Street; Lodi Av. is Main Avenue; Wallington Pl. is Washington Place; Locust Pl. is Lincoln Place; Dankhoff Av. is Dankoff Avenue.
Hathaway Street / Lincoln Place (6.3 m) and Locust Avenue / Strong Street (13 m) were rejected.
Hope, Grant, Elm, New, Wall and Ann streets are in East Rutherford, across Paterson Av.

Garfield volume sheet 25 (Wallington), 100 ft to an inch, turned (north about 36 deg clockwise). One part: Union Pl south past James and King between Paterson Av (East Rutherford line) and Tuttle; Wallington Public School No. 1, Henry W. Plant & Co.

sheet-26-1.description: Main part of sheet 26 of the 1917 Sanborn atlas of Garfield, covering eastern Wallington at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points about 37 degrees clockwise of up. Lodi Av runs along the Passaic River at the top, opposite the City of Passaic, with the Wallington Coal & Ice Co. by the steel bridge at the top left. Below it are Locust Av, Tuttle, Strong and Alden crossed by James and King, then Orchard, James, Adamson and Brook Av, all marked not opened, west of Reservoir Av. The Anderson Chemical Co. works lies along Reservoir Av near Lodi Av. East of it are Park Row, Kossuth, Lexington Av and Wagner with Szepes and Mt. Pleasant Av at the foot, Cross St. and Bergstrom St. by the frame of the detached part. Large parts are platted but unbuilt (blocks 64, 65); dwellings cluster along Park Row, Kossuth and Strong. The foot of the sheet holds a framed detached area (part 2) and a water works inset at 50 feet to an inch (part 3, not placed).
notes: Lodi Av. is today Main Avenue; James is Pulaski Avenue; Szepes is Chestnut Street.

Main Avenue junctions at Reservoir Avenue (7.6 m) and Kossuth Street (14.7 m) were rejected; the riverside Main Avenue appears realigned. Pulaski Avenue / Strong Street and Alden Street / Main Avenue were excluded.
King is drawn 50 ft wide against about 75 ft parcels today; street_widths set.
Firms: Anderson Chemical Co.; Wallington Coal & Ice Co.

Garfield volume sheet 26 (Wallington), 100 ft to an inch, turned like sheet 25. Three parts: part 1 main map (Lodi Av along the Passaic River south to King and Mt. Pleasant Av, Tuttle to Kossuth and Wagner; Anderson Chemical Co.); part 2 detached area framed at the foot (Szepes, Zemplin, Saros, Franklin and Jacobs, east of Wagner Av); part 3 inset lower left at 50 ft to an inch (Municipal Water Works & Pumping Station and reservoir on Spring).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Municipal Water Works & Pumping Station on Spring, 50 ft to an inch (no street junction (Spring is the only street drawn); needs hand-picked control from the reservoir or the Erie R.R. line).

sheet-26-2.description: Detached area framed by a heavy line at the foot of sheet 26 of the 1917 Sanborn atlas of Garfield, in eastern Wallington, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned like the rest of the sheet, with its own arrow. It continues the main map eastward from Wagner Av: Szepes runs east from Wagner Av across Zemplin Av to Saros Av, Jacobs and Park Row cross Saros Av at the top, Franklin Av runs along the east side, and Mt. Pleasant Av closes the area at the foot; Summit St. is marked at the north-east corner. The area is mostly platted lots with a few frame dwellings and sheds on Szepes and Saros Av. The public school on block 67, between Wagner Av and Zemplin Av, is the main building. The sheet's scale bar is drawn across the lower part.
notes: Szepes is today Chestnut Street; Zemplin Av. is Pine Street; Saros Av. is Willow Avenue; Jacobs is Jacob Street.
